speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 但在战术上，我认为好的事情是我们发现 PM 们被解放得更多了。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 因此，他们实际上可以更多地投资于开发关于他们的客户的真正洞察。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're finding out your engineering leaders, engineering team, they're asking you to really confirm your insight and your instinct about the customer.

speaker: Unknown
en: The second thing I would say is that there's a need to orchestrate a little differently.

en: So in the past, it was around people, orchestrating people, getting them into the room, et cetera.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 这个想法是 PM……几乎把更多的时间花在漏斗的顶部、产品生命周期的顶部，确认来自客户数据的洞察，决定构建什么。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 在过去 20 年里，我们就工作如何完成有着非常固定的比例。

speaker: Unknown

zh: PM 花费这么多时间，开发人员花费这么多时间，上市花费这么多时间。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我认为这种契约基本上正在爆炸，因为构建过程，封闭的求解过程，构建过程正在加速得如此之快。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我有一个非常酷的特邀主持人很快就要出来,她教给你的关于如何变得擅长评估的东西比你想象的还要多。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I want to double down on something you just said, which I love so much, which is this idea of instead of waiting to see what jobs AI takes, it's almost like the way you phrased it essentially is what jobs can you take as a PM?
zh: 但我想加倍强调你刚才说的话,我非常喜欢,这个想法是,与其等待看 AI 带走哪些工作,几乎就像你措辞它的那样,基本上是作为 PM 你可以带走哪些工作?

speaker: Unknown
en: What can you do?
zh: 你能做什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you do more engineering?
zh: 你能做更多工程吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you do more design?
zh: 你能做更多设计吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Such an empowering way to think about it.
zh: 这是一种非常赋能的思考方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me talk about something that's really personal and part of the Women in Product organization.
zh: 让我谈谈非常个人的事情,并且是 Women in Product 组织的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was asked to guest write end of last year because there was a lot of fear in the community and there was this thing called the rise of the CTPO.
zh: 去年年底我被邀请客座撰写文章,因为社区里有很多恐惧,并且有这个叫 CTPO 兴起的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's this thing, it's been in the background there where I think many VCs, many PEs were asking, "Do I need a CPO as well as a CTO?"
zh: 就是这个东西,它一直潜伏在背景中,我认为许多 VC,许多 PE 在问,"我是否需要 CPO 以及 CTO?"

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was always amazed at how many people were leaned back in this thing versus actually showing and proving the value of what a CPO could be.
zh: 我总是惊讶于有多少人在这件事上靠后坐,而不是实际展示并证明 CPO 可以具有的价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in many places it is right that maybe you do only want one person, particularly when it's very well-known spaces, right?
zh: 所以在很多地方，确实可能你只想要一个人，尤其是在非常知名的领域，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's clear.
zh: 很清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're not doing anything revolutionary, but it's like saying an engineer is the same as a product person.
zh: 他们没有做任何革命性的事情，但这就像是说工程师和产品人员是一样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you think about it that way, there is a conflict between the CPO and the CTO that actually drives innovation in my opinion, because one person is trying to optimize the resourcing, the fixed, right?
zh: 当你那样想的时候，CPO 和 CTO 之间确实存在一种冲突，我认为这实际上推动了创新，因为一个人试图优化资源，优化固定的东西，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: While another person is actually trying to field opportunities and figure out how to wait and decide what is best to do it.
zh: 而另一个人实际上试图在场上寻找机会，弄清楚如何等待并决定做什么是最好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the higher level, those are their jobs.
zh: 在更高层次上，这些就是他们的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that tension is really good because you need them to sharpen each other as you try to maximize the value of the organization.
zh: 这种张力真的很好，因为当你试图最大化组织的价值时，你需要他们互相磨砺。

speaker: Unknown
en: I say all this to say that there are folks who are not stopping to figure out, "how do we make the pie bigger?"
zh: 我说这些是为了说明，有些人没有停下来思考，“我们如何把蛋糕做大？”

speaker: Unknown
en: But they're looking at instead, "How do we divide this pie as it gets smaller?"
zh: 而是在看，“当蛋糕变小时，我们要如何分配这块蛋糕？”

speaker: Unknown
en: Versus asking the question of really, what is the opportunity to increase this for all of us?
zh: 而不是问这个问题，对我们所有人来说，增加这个的机会到底是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is a skill set I also look out for.
zh: 这也是我关注的一种技能组合。

speaker: Unknown
en: Awesome.
zh: 很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to go to Oji in a second, but I want to come back on this humble idea.
zh: 我马上就要让 Oji 发言了，但我想回到这个谦卑的想法上。

speaker: Unknown
en: I haven't heard this before.
zh: 我以前没听说过这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why do you find it really important for people to be humble?
zh: 为什么你觉得人们保持谦卑真的很重要？

speaker: Unknown
en: I haven't heard that piece of advice yet.
zh: 我还没听过那条建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh my gosh.
zh: 天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: Particularly now, it is really important to be, because I would say, "Okay, I went to school, I actually did neural networks in school when I was doing a project."
zh: 特别是现在，保持谦卑真的很重要，因为我会说，“好吧，我上过学，我在学校做项目时实际上做过神经网络。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And you get to this part of your career where you go, "I kind of know a lot of what product is."
zh: 你会到达职业生涯的这个阶段，你会想，“我确实知道很多产品是什么。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I do see folks who are not willing to go sign up for that new junior AI PMs course because they're a CPO or they're a head of product or they're XY or Z, or they're a principal PM now.
zh: 我确实看到有些人不愿意去报名参加那个新的初级 AI PM 课程，因为他们是 CPO，或者是产品负责人，或者是 XY 或 Z，或者是现在的首席 PM。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that that's a mistake.
zh: 我认为这是一个错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that it's important to realize that you don't know everything.
zh: 我认为意识到你并不是无所不知很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't know everything.
zh: 你不可能无所不知。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even as a leader, CPO, head of product, et cetera, I come from this school where I believe that in order to lead an organization, sometimes you actually do need to know how to do the work and I think I lead better that way.
zh: 即使作为领导者、CPO、产品负责人等等，我来自这样一个学派，我认为为了领导一个组织，有时你确实需要知道如何做这项工作，我认为我那样领导得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So being able to sign up and say, "You know what, let me sit in and figure out how we're going to build this thing."
zh: 所以能够报名并说，“你知道吗，让我坐下来弄清楚我们要如何构建这个东西。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And number one, learn for yourself, but also figure out what questions other PMs are asking in that course, right?
zh: 第一，自己学习，但也要弄清楚其他 PM 在那个课程中在问什么问题，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's about taking courses from people you may have considered junior, figuring out and sitting and reading books that you thought... Just going back to the day one of, "How do you build product in an AI world?"
zh: 所以这是关于从你可能认为资历较浅的人那里上课，弄清楚并坐下来阅读那些你曾以为……的书。只是回到第一天，“在 AI 世界中你如何构建产品？”

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's where humility comes to play in this period where we are.
zh: 所以这就是谦卑在我们这个时期发挥作用的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just don't know everything, can't know everything and things will change faster than you're able to stay ahead of.
zh: 你就是不能什么都懂，不可能什么都懂，而且事物变化的速度超过你能保持领先的速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: So lean on your team as well.
zh: 所以也要依靠你的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just had this guy, Chip Conley on the podcast.
zh: 我刚邀请了 Chip Conley 上播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's in his 60s.
zh: 他六十多岁了。

speaker: Unknown
en: He joined Airbnb when he was 52 as an intern and he said exactly the same thing to be successful.
zh: 他 52 岁时以实习生的身份加入了 Airbnb，他说为了成功，完全是一回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's interesting as a metaphor, as an older person, you need to be really good at being open to learning from people younger than you.
zh: 这很有趣，作为一个隐喻，作为一个年长者，你需要非常擅长向比你年轻的人学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's a really interesting, I think lens and heuristic almost for just people that aren't as AI savvy yet just leaning into that idea of just like, "Okay, I can actually learn a lot from people around me even if they're much younger than me."
zh: 这是一个非常有趣的，我认为视角和启发式方法，几乎适用于那些对 AI 还不太精通的人，只是倾向于这个想法，就像，“好吧，即使他们比我年轻得多，我实际上也可以从周围的人那里学到很多东西。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So Oji, something else that I think that you're really good at and you've been spending time on that I think is also really important is getting super hands-on with the tech, not just reading and not just listening to podcasts like this.
zh: 所以 Oji，我认为你非常擅长并且花时间在做另一件事，我认为也非常重要的是，对技术变得超级动手实践，不仅仅是阅读，也不仅仅是听像这样的播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not just reading newsletters but actually building stuff.
zh: 不仅仅是阅读通讯，而是实际构建东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about just why that's important, and what you've been doing to learn and to stay ahead and not just be a pontificator guy in the clouds.
zh: 谈谈为什么这很重要，以及你一直在做什么来学习和保持领先，而不仅仅是做一个云端的空谈者。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just love everything we've said in the last few minutes.
zh: 我只是喜欢我们在过去几分钟里说的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the shorthand I have for humility is humility is teachability.
zh: 我对谦卑的简略说法是，谦卑就是可教性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when do you need teachability?
zh: 什么时候你需要可教性？

speaker: Unknown
en: You need teachability when everything has changed, where there is no blueprint and whatever you think is a blueprint of AI in the last few years, whether, "Oh wow, Lovable is so successful.
zh: 当一切都改变了，没有蓝图时，你需要可教性，无论你在过去几年认为什么是 AI 的蓝图，无论是，“噢哇，Lovable 太成功了。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Replit is so successful."
zh: Replit 太成功了。”

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually quite possible that any one of those companies won't be around in two, three years, right?
zh: 实际上这些公司中的任何一家在两三年后都可能不存在了，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because we're still writing the playbook for what success looks like.
zh: 因为我们仍在编写关于成功看起来是什么样的的剧本。

speaker: Unknown
en: So humility is teachability and teachability is survivability, if you are thinking about careers.
zh: 所以谦卑就是可教性，如果你考虑职业生涯的话，可教性就是生存能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also if you are thinking about building something that's important is also important like that.
zh: 如果你在考虑构建重要的东西，这也是重要的，就像那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: In terms of how to keep your hands sharp, what I would say is a couple of things.
zh: 关于如何保持你的手敏锐，我要说的是几点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ezinne and I both have a master's in engineering, but we very quickly figured out that the thing that we were gifted at was helping to invent the future.
zh: Ezinne 和我都有工程学硕士学位，但我们很快发现我们 gifted 的东西是帮助发明未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are customers thinking?
zh: 客户在想什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we work with developers to do that?
zh: 我们如何与开发者合作来做到这一点？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we've been PMs forever and being a PM means that even though we could, we don't write code, we work with developers, we work with other people in the market, but I've written more code in the last one year than I have in the last 10 years because code is now essentially architecture and English or whatever language that you have.
zh: 我们一直是 PM（产品经理），做 PM 意味着即使我们可以，我们也不写代码，我们与开发者合作，我们与市场上的其他人合作，但在过去一年里，我写的代码比我过去 10 年写的还要多，因为代码现在本质上是架构和英语或你拥有的任何语言。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what does that mean?
zh: 那么这意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I've taken the opportunity to write more code, I've taken the opportunity to convert PRD writing into prototype writing.
zh: 我抓住了这个机会写更多代码，我抓住了这个机会把写 PRD（产品需求文档）转变为写原型。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've taken the opportunity to write more API interfaces and actually call those API interfaces with Postman myself.
zh: 我抓住了这个机会编写更多 API 接口，并亲自用 Postman 调用那些 API 接口。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've taken the opportunity to subscribe to all the AI tools and take that as a cost of learning so that I can understand what each model is useful for.
zh: 我抓住了这个机会订阅所有的 AI 工具，并将这视为学习的成本，这样我就能理解每个模型适用于什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've taken the opportunity to understand MCPs and connect different things to it.
zh: 我抓住了这个机会去理解 MCPs 并将不同的东西连接到它上面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right now, one of my pet projects, one of the things I do in order to learn is I pick a project that it's almost like writing an eval.
zh: 现在，我的个人项目之一，我为了学习而做的一件事是，我会选择一个项目，这几乎就像是在编写一个 eval（评估）。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was an eval for my life to learn, is I'll pick a project that touches a lot of the things that I need to learn that I'm interested and passionate about.
zh: 这是我生活中的一个 eval，用于学习，就是我会选择一个触及我需要学习的很多东西的项目，我对这些感兴趣且充满热情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as I get into it, because of my passion, I start to learn more and more.
zh: 当我深入其中时，因为我的热情，我开始学得越来越多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, one of the passion projects I have is to automate my house.
zh: 所以，我的热情项目之一就是自动化我的房子。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I've been doing this for years and years, but now I'm trying to build a very smart house, run on a processor that has AI chip and inference in it while the house looks dumb because I don't want anyone to know about it.
zh: 我已经做这件事很多年了，但现在我试图建立一个非常智能的房子，运行在一个带有 AI 芯片和推理（inference）功能的处理器上，同时房子看起来很笨，因为我不希望任何人知道这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what am I doing?
zh: 那么我在做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm getting models.
zh: 我在获取模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am learning about what quantization of those models means.
zh: 我在了解那些模型的量化（quantization）意味着什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am learning how to fine tune some of them.
zh: 我在学习如何微调（fine tune）其中一些模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm feeding them and build an MCP server in my house that talks to the home entities and then I can collaborate with Claude on how to build and make it sort of super dynamic.
zh: 我在喂养它们，并在家里建立一个 MCP 服务器，它与家居实体对话，然后我可以与 Claude 协作如何构建并使其变得超级动态。

speaker: Unknown
en: But beyond that, one of the things we're spending time on is a venture studio and raising capital for a venture studio because that's what I want to spend the next decade on building seminal AI companies beyond the book.
zh: 但除此之外，我们花时间做的一件事是建立一家创投工作室（venture studio）并为这家创投工作室筹集资金，因为那是我想在未来十年致力于建设开创性 AI 公司的事情，除了写书之外。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm collaborating with some of the smartest people in AI right now who can teach me how to do this, how to write agents, what agents really mean.
zh: 我正在与目前 AI 领域的一些最聪明的人合作，他们可以教我如何做到这一点，如何编写智能体，智能体真正意味着什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, everything Ezinne said, writing evals, being humble, going back after 25 years of being a PM to being teachable is how I stay sharp.
zh: 所以，Ezinne 说的每一件事，编写 evals，保持谦逊，在做了 25 年 PM 之后重新变得可教，这就是我保持敏锐的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to go back to this house.
zh: 我想回到这个房子的话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is your house doing?
zh: 你的房子在做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: How smart is this house?
zh: 这个房子有多智能？

speaker: Unknown
en: The idea is that I give the house eyes and ears and it senses... The coolest thing is I've specced out what I call a super sensor.
zh: 想法是我给房子眼睛和耳朵，它能感知……最酷的是我已经规划了我所谓的超级传感器。

speaker: Unknown
en: It will see people, it'll feel their heat, it'll hear them, it'll sense humidity and temperature and it'll just be scattered around the house, right?
zh: 它会看到人，会感觉到他们的热量，会听到他们，会感知湿度和温度，它就会分散在房子周围，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm building the hardware myself.
zh: 我正在自己构建硬件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And basically as you walk into the house, it starts to adapts itself to you.
zh: 基本上当你走进房子时，它开始为你适应自身。

speaker: Unknown
en: It manages energy in the house.
zh: 它管理房子里的能源。

speaker: Unknown
en: It knows you're in a room.
zh: 它知道你在一个房间里。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you leave... My kids are not in their rooms right now.
zh: 如果你离开……我的孩子们现在不在他们的房间里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, the HVAC around them just stopped and said, "Oh, they're not here."
zh: 嗯，他们周围的 HVAC（暖通空调）刚刚停止了，并说：“噢，他们不在那里。”

speaker: Unknown
en: An hour before they come back, it starts to pre-cool their space.
zh: 在他们回来的一小时前，它开始预冷他们的空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then when they come back it says, "Oh, they're here."
zh: 当他们回来时，它说：“噢，他们在这里。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And it starts to do cool things.
zh: 然后它开始做很酷的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a lot of stuff like that that I'm building.
zh: 所以我正在构建很多类似的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the question is you don't want that to be completely inflexible.
zh: 问题是，你不希望那是完全不可改变的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want it to be super dynamic and superhuman.
zh: 你希望它是超级动态的和超人的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's part of the AI.
zh: 所以这是 AI 的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am the recipient of all of this.
zh: 我是这一切的接受者。

speaker: Unknown
en: I woke up at one AM and I want toast.
zh: 我在凌晨一点醒来，想吃吐司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is the toast not working?
zh: 为什么吐司机不工作？

speaker: Unknown
en: Wait, hold on.
zh: 等等，稍等。

zh: 那是因为他切断了食品储藏室的电源。

en: It's not good for you.
zh: 这对你不好。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why.
zh: 这就是原因。

en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

en: No, but look, Ezinne walks into lots of rooms in the house and the light just turns on and when she leaves, she just walks out and then it knows she's not there and it turns it off and she's taking it for granted.
zh: 不，但是看，Ezinne 走进房子里的很多房间，灯就亮了，当她离开时，她只是走出去，然后它知道她不在那里了，就会把它关掉，而她觉得这是理所当然的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wait, it's actually doing all this?
zh: 等等，它实际上真的在做所有这些吗？

en: Wow.

en: It is.

en: Yes, there is.
zh: 是的，有。

en: Definitely.

zh: 我想说的是，我的家人不应该惹恼我，因为我可以对它们做疯狂的事情。

en: That's all I'll say.
zh: 我就说这么多。

en: Oh, man.

en: Is that what the power is?
zh: 这就是力量所在吗？

en: So multiple levels.
zh: 所以有多个层面。

en: There's this open source software called Home Assistant that I use and you can... It's very extensible.

en: So I can fine-tuned LLMs, I can use the big LLMs.
zh: 所以我可以微调 LLM，我可以使用大型 LLM。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the things that we don't see people doing actually that we want people to do is something Ezinne mentioned, which is ethics.
zh: 实际上有一件事我们没看到人们在做的，是我们希望人们做的，就是 Ezinne 提到的那件事，也就是道德。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think of AI and its core capabilities as ordnance level, meaning... At some point we'll think of this as more powerful than the fusion bomb.
zh: 我们认为 AI 及其核心能力是军械级别的，意思是……在某个时候我们会认为这比核弹更强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have a bunch of software people who have no consideration of ethics play with this stuff all the time.
zh: 我们有一群软件人员，他们根本没有考虑道德，一直在玩这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, one thing we'd like to see the best companies do is lead on that.
zh: 所以，我们希望看到最好的公司做的一件事就是在这方面领先。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think about the responsibility we have to the human race when we build new digital products, I will give them superpowers.
zh: 思考一下当我们构建新的数字产品时，我们对人类所负的责任，我会给他们超能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to zoom out even further.
zh: 我想进一步拉远视角。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we started talking about individual people skills, what's going to be most important.
zh: 所以我们开始谈论个人技能，什么是最重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've been talking just now about what companies are doing well, the ones that are succeeding in this crazy new world of AI.
zh: 我们刚才一直在谈论公司做得好的地方，那些在这个疯狂的 AI 新世界中成功的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to now zoom out just your entire product career.
zh: 现在我想拉远到你的整个产品职业生涯。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious, just when you look back at the 50 plus years of combined experience you two have, what are some of the biggest product lessons that you've learned that you would love to share, that you think people can avoid having to learn the hard way?
zh: 我很好奇，当你回顾你们两人加起来 50 多年的经验时，你学到了哪些最大的产品经验，你很乐意分享，你认为人们可以避免必须以艰难的方式去学习？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think what I want to reiterate, the thing that we talked about, sharp problems.
zh: 我想我想重申我们谈到的这一点，尖锐的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem you focus on is probably the most predictive of your success.
zh: 你关注的问题可能是你成功的最预测性因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pick a sharp problem, pick something that if you really solve it, people will come.
zh: 选择一个尖锐的问题，选择一些如果你真的解决了它，人们就会来的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Watching Jeff Bezos from the 80s feels prescient.
zh: 回看 80 年代的 Jeff Bezos 感觉很有先见之明。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's like, "Look, people always shop.
zh: 他就像，「看，人们总是购物。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to be the guy."
zh: 我会成为那个人。」

speaker: Unknown
en: And he did it.
zh: 他做到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So do that.
zh: 所以去做吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I say this humbly because I've failed because sometimes we build things that we are passionate about, but being a founder is not an exercise and even an operator in a company, it's not an exercise in your passion and your brilliance.
zh: 我谦虚地说这一点，因为我曾经失败过，因为有时我们构建我们热衷的东西，但作为创始人甚至公司里的运营者，这不是在你的激情和你的才华上的练习。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's an exercise in finding what the market needs.
zh: 这是发现市场需要的练习。

speaker: Unknown
en: So do that, be disciplined in doing that.
zh: 所以这样做，在这样做上要有纪律。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also talk about simplicity a lot.
zh: 我们也经常谈论简单性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even this morning I was talking to a designer and he had a convoluted user experience and I said, "Only 20% of people who come to this will see that."
zh: 就在今天早上，我在和一位设计师交谈，他有一个复杂的用户体验，我说：“只有 20% 来这里的人会看到那个。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the point of design is first, simplicity and clarity before we get fancy.
zh: 因此，设计的要点首先是，在我们追求花哨之前，要先做到简单和清晰。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's a lot... Steve Jobs embodied this earlier on.
zh: 所以有很多……史蒂夫·乔布斯早年就体现了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think iOS has become complicated, but start with simplicity and simple is hard.
zh: 我认为 iOS 已经变得复杂了，但要从简单开始，而简单是很难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in 2025 we're designing for distracted brains.
zh: 在 2025 年，我们要为分心的大脑进行设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: A couple of things are happening.
zh: 有几件事正在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: People are super distracted.
zh: 人们超级分心。

speaker: Unknown
en: People are no longer wowed by technology, call it AI all you want.
zh: 人们不再对技术感到惊叹，随你怎么叫它（AI）。

speaker: Unknown
en: They just assume that it is what it is.
zh: 他们只是认为它就是它现在的样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so simplicity is really good for 2025 and beyond basically.
zh: 因此，简单对于 2025 年及以后真的很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we talk a lot about fundamentals.
zh: 然后我们经常谈论基础知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to throw this to Ezinne.
zh: 我要把这个交给 Ezinne。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are ways to figure out the fundamentals.
zh: 有方法可以搞清楚这些基础知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know we operate in the software layer, but it's most basic.
zh: 我知道我们在软件层运作，但这是最基础的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're trying to predict what humans would do, what they'll want, how their workflow will go.
zh: 我们试图预测人类会做什么，他们会想要什么，他们的工作流程会如何进行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a layer of that that is quite similar because our friends, the anthropologists and the psychologists really understand this.
zh: 其中有一部分是非常相似的，因为我们的朋友，人类学家和心理学家真的理解这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think if we understand it, we can build better software.
zh: 我认为如果我们理解了这一点，我们就能构建更好的软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: But Ezinne I'm just going to throw this off to you so I don't take up all the space.
zh: 但是 Ezinne，我就把这个抛给你，这样我就不会占满所有的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go for it.
zh: 请讲。

speaker: Ezinne Udezue
en: No, I think you're onto something about just... So when I think about the hard lessons I've learned, you talked about simplicity, and I'm saying this also from humility and just having learned a lot from past failures. One of the reasons people create complicated solutions is because they're afraid to take a stab, to put their point of view out there, right?
zh: 不，我觉得你刚才说到了点子上……所以当我想到我学到的惨痛教训时，你谈到了简单，我是带着谦卑以及从过去的失败中学到很多东西来说这话的。人们创建复杂解决方案的原因之一是因为他们不敢尝试，不敢把他们的观点表达出来，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: They're not opinionated.
zh: 他们没有观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're not opinionated enough.
zh: 他们的观点不够鲜明。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that often comes from not having high conviction because you're not sure that you've spent the time with the customer.
zh: 这通常是因为没有强烈的信念，因为你不确定你在客户身上花了足够的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: So with that, I know it sounds trite, but spend time and understand the customer or borrow from others who do.
zh: 因此，我知道这听起来很老套，但要花时间并理解客户，或者从其他理解客户的人那里借鉴。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you've got to not just lay it all out and have them choose which way because it is so effing confusing.
zh: 但是你绝不能把所有东西都摊开让他们选哪条路，因为这太他妈令人困惑了。

speaker: Unknown
en: 10,000 options because you can't pick one.
zh: 一万个选项，因为你选不出一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The experience is so murky, chalky, nobody knows what the hell to do because you can't make a decision.
zh: 这种体验太浑浊、不清爽，没人知道该做什么，因为你做不出决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: Make it simple.
zh: 让它变得简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Come up with an opinion and put your opinion out there.
zh: 提出一个观点并把你的观点表达出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can change.
zh: 你可以改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: Leave the configurations and the options behind, but leave them behind the scenes if you must.
zh: 把配置和选项留在后面，如果必须的话就把它们留在幕后。

speaker: Unknown
en: But try and create the most compelling, the simplest experience and you will actually have better adoption.
zh: 但要试着创造最引人注目、最简单的体验，这样你实际上会有更好的采用率。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're better off doing that and being wrong.
zh: 你最好这样做，哪怕做错了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many times we leave and ship convoluted experiences because we don't have the courage, number one to make a decision, create a point of view and ship it out there.
zh: 许多时候，我们交付复杂的体验是因为我们没有勇气，第一，没有勇气做出决定，创建一个观点并把它发布出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: The reality is, and my experience has shown that, you're better off picking an opinion, shipping it out there, being wrong, and then adjusting than leaving too many options because you then can never learn what was the better experience overall.
zh: 现实是，我的经验也表明了这一点，你最好选择一个观点，把它发布出去，做错了，然后再调整，而不是留下太多的选项，因为那样你就永远无法学到整体上什么是更好的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's one thing.
zh: 所以这是其中一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other major lesson I've learned is actually one about strategy.
zh: 我学到的另一个主要教训实际上是关于战略的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is that the best way to go from strategy to execution in a way that activates the entire organization is communication.
zh: 就是以一种激活整个组织的方式从战略走向执行的最佳途径是沟通。

speaker: Unknown
en: You will never spend too much time communicating the why to your organization over and over and over again.
zh: 在向你的组织一遍又一遍地传达“为什么”这方面，你花的时间永远不过分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't remember what movie it was, I think it was the movie about sending someone to the moon, right?
zh: 我不记得那是部电影了，我想是那部关于把人送上月球的电影，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm forgetting what it is, but the idea that everybody in NASA knew that we were working to send a man to the moon, even the janitor knew that.
zh: 我忘了那是什么，但这个想法是，NASA 的每个人都知道我们要致力于把一个人送上月球，甚至连看门人都知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that idea of ensuring that everybody in the team understands the why behind what we're doing and can speak to it.
zh: 所以这种确保团队中的每个人都理解我们要做的事情背后的“为什么”，并能谈论它的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I saw something on LinkedIn the other day.
zh: 前几天我在 LinkedIn 上看到了一些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it was Martin Erickson who actually posted this.
zh: 我想那是 Martin Erickson 发布的这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: It talked about how the same way we talk about crossing the chasm and figuring out who it is that will adopt a product, we should think about the change management required for strategy communication through that lens.
zh: 它谈到了同样的方式，我们谈论跨越鸿沟并找出谁会采用产品，我们应该通过那个镜头来思考战略沟通所需的变革管理。

speaker: Unknown
en: There will be early adopters.
zh: 会有早期采用者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think about those people.
zh: 想想那些人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those people will hear the message, the strategy.
zh: 那些人会听到信息、战略。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the time others are just beginning to understand what it is, they're probably on the next version of the strategy asking, "What can change?
zh: 等到其他人刚刚开始理解它是什么时，他们可能已经在讨论下一版战略了，在问“什么可以改变？”

speaker: Unknown
en: What should change?"
zh: 什么应该改变？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was so clarifying for me because I always wondered why strategy could get muddy sometimes is because when you look at your entire population, about 5% are going to be the early adopters.
zh: 这对我来说非常清晰，因为我一直想知道为什么战略有时会变得混乱，是因为当你审视你的整个群体时，大约有 5% 的人将是早期采用者。

speaker: Unknown
en: They get it.
zh: 他们懂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They buy into it and they're moving.
zh: 他们认同并且他们在行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Four months later they're onto something wondering what the next version of the strategy will look like, how do we build on top of this?
zh: 四个月后他们已经在做别的事了，想知道战略的下一个版本会是什么样，我们要如何在此基础之上构建？

speaker: Unknown
en: At that same time, some people are just beginning to get it.
zh: 与此同时，有些人才刚刚开始理解它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And honestly, that answered a lot of questions for me as to how it is that you can be working on a strategy, some people get it, can recite it, tell you why we're doing what we're doing, while some PMs are still struggling with, "But why?
zh: 老实说，这为我解答了很多问题，关于你怎么能在做一个战略时，有些人懂了，能复述它，告诉你我们为什么要做我们所做的，而有些产品经理还在纠结，「但是为什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: How come?
zh: 怎么会？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can we do this?"
zh: 我们能做这个吗？」

speaker: Unknown
en: Because they are in fact laggards out there.
zh: 因为他们实际上是落后者。

speaker: Unknown
en: That idea of trying to really activate a strategy into pure execution, if you think about communication as a critical element, and then also look at it as, "What is the crossing the chasm version?
zh: 试图真正激活一个战略进入纯执行的想法，如果你把沟通视为一个关键要素，然后也把它看作，「什么是跨越鸿沟的版本？

speaker: Unknown
en: Who is at what point in this change management journey?"
zh: 谁在这个变革管理旅程的哪个点？」

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that was one of the major lessons I've learned as a leader in product.
zh: 我认为这是我作为产品领导者学到的最重要的一课之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love these sorts of conversations where you two spend 50 years learning and then you just tell us, "Here's all the answers.
zh: 我喜欢这种类型的对话，你们花了 50 年学习，然后你们就告诉我们，「这是所有的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's a bunch of stuff that'll save you a bunch of pain and suffering."
zh: 这是一堆能省去你们很多痛苦和折磨的东西。」

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me try to summarize what you shared and tell me what I missed.
zh: 让我试着总结一下你们分享的，告诉我我遗漏了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So some of the biggest things you two have learned over the past 50 years and all, it's not in the right order, but communicating the why and you can never spend too much time helping people understand why what you're working on is important.
zh: 所以你们两人在过去 50 年里学到的一些最重要的东西，顺序不对，但是沟通「为什么」，你永远花不了太多时间去帮助人们理解你们正在做的东西为什么是重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's just the change management component of not underestimating the work that it'll take to convince people to adopt something.
zh: 然后还有变革管理的部分，不要低估说服人们采用某样东西所需要的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then this whole idea of crossing the chasm, we had Geoffrey Moore on the podcast, so we'll point to that if you want to deeply understand what that's all about.
zh: 然后是跨越鸿沟的整个概念，我们请过 Geoffrey Moore 上播客，所以如果你想深入理解那是关于什么的，我们会指向那一期。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then this lesson of simplicity, just the value of keeping things simple, easier said than done.
zh: 然后是关于简单化的这一课，就是保持事物简单的价值，说起来容易做起来难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And having an opinion, having the courage almost to do something really simple, not give people all the options.
zh: 以及拥有一个观点，拥有那种勇气去做真正简单的事情，而不给人们所有的选项。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then Oji, you talked about the idea of most times when something fails, you're going after the wrong problem, it's not sharp enough or it's just not solving something people actually care about.
zh: 然后 Oji，你谈到了这个观点，大多数时候当某件事失败时，你是在解决错误的问题，它不够尖锐，或者它只是没有解决人们真正关心的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then just talking to customers.
zh: 然后就是和客户交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Always easy to say.
zh: 总是说起来很容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most people don't actually do it enough.
zh: 大多数人实际上做得不够。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to add one more thing and I'll be brief.
zh: 我想再加一件事，我会简短点。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is more about people's careers, like PMs.
zh: 这更多是关于人们的职业生涯，比如产品经理。

speaker: Unknown
en: In our career, we started out as engineers basically, became mainline PMs, got an MBA, worked harder, became executives, and so on and so forth.
zh: 在我们的职业生涯中，我们基本上是从工程师开始的，成为主线产品经理，读了 MBA，更努力工作，成为高管，等等等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: So some people look at it, my career and Ezi's career, and they're like, "Oh, this is amazing."
zh: 所以有些人看它，我和 Ezi 的职业生涯，他们会说，「噢，这太棒了。」

speaker: Unknown
en: But behind that is a lot of intention.
zh: 但在那背后是有很多意图的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We always held in our brains, "What do we want to do next?
zh: 我们的大脑里总是想着，「我们下一步想做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the next step?
zh: 下一步是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the hunger that drives us?"
zh: 什么是驱动我们的渴望？」

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's nothing more powerful than intention, than imagination.
zh: 没有什么比意图和想象力更强大的了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like a little bit of cheese in front of the mouse, it chases after.
zh: 这就像老鼠前面的一小块奶酪，它会去追逐。

speaker: Unknown
en: Being able to visualize and chase the thing that you see about where you want to be is so powerful.
zh: 能够想象并追逐你关于你想在哪里的愿景，是如此强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: I talked to a guy who gave me a break.
zh: 我和一个给我机会的人聊过。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when I was the last two years of my time at Microsoft, I switched to become a marketing lead because I was a little tired of PM at Microsoft specifically, and I was getting an MBA.
zh: 所以当我在微软的最后两年时，我转岗成为一名市场负责人，因为我有点厌倦了微软的产品经理，我当时正在读 MBA。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I talked to Dave Mendlen, he was vice president or senior director in... And worked eventually for Satya and he gave me a break and became a product marketer over a couple of years.
zh: 我和 Dave Mendlen 谈过，他是副总裁还是总监……最后为 Satya 工作，他给了我机会，在几年时间里成为了一名产品营销人员。

speaker: Unknown
en: But he came back and talked to me this year and he said, "Oji, everything you told me you wanted to do from afar, I saw that you have done and you told me about them 10 years ago."
zh: 但他今年回来跟我谈话，他说，「Oji，你从远处告诉我你想做的一切，我看到你都做了，而且你是 10 年前告诉我的。」

speaker: Unknown
en: And I didn't even know that.
zh: 而我甚至都不知道那件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's a very powerful thing.
zh: 所以这是一件非常有力的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that this is not just about how to build better products, but how to manage your own career is super important.
zh: 我认为这不仅仅是关于如何构建更好的产品，如何管理你自己的职业生涯也是超级重要的。

speaker: Lenny
en: I just went to a storytelling event and there was a very similar theme. This guy just always wanted to be a stand-up comedian. And the lesson he learned is just the best motivator is desire. Having that desire not fade because that'll... It's kind of like going back to our idea of the project. Having a project to work on because you need a problem solved is a really good way to just get to where you want to go.
zh: 我刚去了一个讲故事的活动，有一个非常相似的主题。这家伙一直想成为一名单口喜剧演员。他学到的教训就是最好的动力就是欲望。拥有那种欲望不消退，因为那会……这有点像回到我们要项目的想法。拥有一个项目去工作，因为你需要解决一个问题，这是一个真正到达你想去的地方的好方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ezinne, I think you had something else you wanted to add.
zh: Ezinne，我想你还有些东西想补充。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You said this thing about know the customer, know the customer, and I think there's a lot of noise out there about customer interviews, et cetera, right?
